content: Ethinyl estradiol levels or effects can be altered by various drugs through mechanisms such as hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism, P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter, or receptor binding competition. These interactions can lead to either an increase or decrease in the efficacy of hormonal contraceptives, necessitating careful monitoring, therapy modification, or the use of alternative or additional non-hormonal contraceptive methods. Below are the detailed interactions: 1. Primidone: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use alternative contraception or avoid co-administration. 2. Quinidine: Increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 3. Ranolazine: Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of ranolazine by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Repotrectinib: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use effective non-hormonal contraception. 5. Rifabutin, Rifampin, Rifapentine: Decrease the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use non-hormonal contraception. 6. Ritonavir: Causes significant changes in estrogen plasma levels (increase or decrease). Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. St. John’s Wort: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use non-hormonal contraception. 8. Sugammadex: Decreases the effects of ethinyl estradiol by receptor binding competition. A bolus dose of sugammadex is equivalent to missing doses of hormonal contraceptives. Use additional non-hormonal contraception for 7 days. 9. Tipranavir: Causes significant changes in estrogen plasma levels (increase or decrease). Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use non-hormonal contraception. 10. Topiramate: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Hormonal contraceptive efficacy may be reduced. Use non-hormonal contraception. 11. Tovorafenib: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration. If unavoidable, use additional non-hormonal contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuation. 12. Tucatinib: Increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid co-administration with CYP3A substrates. If unavoidable, reduce the dose of CYP3A substrates. 13. Desogestrel: Decreases the effects of albiglutide by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance. Monitor glycemic control in diabetic patients. 14. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases the level or effect of alosetron by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 15. Atazanavir: May increase or decrease levels of desogestrel by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternatives if available. 16. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases the level or effect of alprazolam by decreasing metabolism. Monitor for increased benzodiazepine serum concentrations. 17. Ethinyl estradiol and aminocaproic acid: Concomitant use may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Monitor for clotting risks. 18. Amoxicillin, Ampicillin: Decrease the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 19. Artemether/Lumefantrine: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 20. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases the level or effect of atogepant by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 21. Atorvastatin: Increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting P-glycoprotein efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 22. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases levels of axitinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases levels of bendamustine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Monitor for increased plasma concentrations of bendamustine. 24. Berotralstat: Increases levels of desogestrel by increasing exposure to etonogestrel, the active metabolite. Weigh risks and benefits of concurrent use. 25. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases the level or effect of caffeine by inhibiting CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 26. Carbamazepine: Decreases the level or effect of desogestrel by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use alternative contraception during and for 28 days after discontinuation. 27. Cefaclor, Cefadroxil, Cefazolin, Cefdinir, Cefepime, Cefepime/Enmetazobactam, Cefixime, Cefotaxime, Cefprozil, Ceftazidime, Ceftibuten, Cefuroxime, Cephalexin: Decrease the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 28. Cenobamate: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use additional or alternative non-hormonal contraception. 29. Ceritinib: Increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 30. Chloramphenicol: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 31. Cimetidine: Increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 32. Ciprofloxacin: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 33. Clarithromycin: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Clindamycin: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 35. Clobazam: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use additional non-hormonal contraception. 36. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases the level or effect of clonazepam by decreasing metabolism. Monitor for increased benzodiazepine serum concentrations. 37. Desogestrel and Exenatide: Oral contraceptives may impair glucose tolerance. Advise patients to take oral contraceptives at least 1 hour before exenatide. 38. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases levels of cyclosporine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor. 39. Dabrafenib: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Danicopan: Increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by increasing plasma concentrations of BCRP substrates. Consider dose reduction of BCRP substrates. 41. Darunavir: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use non-hormonal contraception. 42. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases the level or effect of dasatinib by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 43. Deferasirox: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 44. Demeclocycline: Decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Low risk of contraceptive failure. Use caution and monitor. 45. Ethinyl estradiol: Increases the level or effect of diazepam by decreasing metabolism. Monitor for increased benzodiazepine serum concentrations. This list highlights the importance of understanding drug interactions with ethinyl estradiol to ensure contraceptive efficacy and patient safety.
